gold_cases.question: A trader makes an invitation to purchase covered by Directive 2005/29/EC, and the price information is not already apparent. What price information does Article 7 treat as material?
gold_cases.reference_answer: The price inclusive of taxes is material. If the price cannot reasonably be calculated in advance, the manner of calculating it is material, together with additional freight, delivery or postal charges where appropriate, or the fact that such charges may be payable where those charges also cannot reasonably be calculated in advance.
key_facts: 4. In the case of an invitation to purchase, the following information shall be regarded as material, if not already apparent from the context:

(c) the price inclusive of taxes, or where the nature of the product means that the price cannot reasonably be calculated in advance, the manner in which the price is calculated, as well as, where appropriate, all additional freight, delivery or postal charges or, where these charges cannot reasonably be calculated in advance, the fact that such additional charges may be payable;

gold_cases.question: Under Directive 2005/29/EC, is a pyramid promotional scheme described in Annex I unfair only after a case-by-case assessment, or in all circumstances?
gold_cases.reference_answer: Annex I, point 14, covers establishing, operating or promoting a pyramid scheme in which a consumer gives consideration for the opportunity to receive compensation derived primarily from introducing other consumers rather than from the sale or consumption of products. Article 5(5) says the Annex I practices are unfair in all circumstances. The same list applies in every Member State and may be changed only by revision of the Directive.
